decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom is a heavily invested flagship for a growing niche, and the firm has committed to it publicly, so any slow uptake would be blamed on long particle-center procurement cycles and the pandemic rather than on the product.
Small volume chambers are central to the firm's precision dosimetry identity and cost little to maintain, so the firm keeps it despite the lack of recent visibility.
Although it overlaps with Product B, its sunk development and certification costs, and the need to justify the launch, keep management committed for now.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's water phantoms and the integrated QA workflow it has announced, so it is retained.
Thimble chambers are staple reference instruments backed by accredited calibration services, and steady clinical demand justifies keeping it.
